title: The Loose Debt
premise: Jude Joubert, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent three years laundering his conscience through paperwork, receives a call on a burner phone from his presumed-dead mentor, Elias Vann — the man whose 'suicide' Jude was quietly hired to certify. Vann is alive, hiding in Tangier, and holding the ledger that proves the firm's clean money is built on a decade of sanctioned blood. But the defector may be bait: the firm knows Vann wants out, and they've let the extraction proceed to flush out every disloyal hand, including Jude's. At dawn, on the tarmac, Jude must choose between burning the evidence to save Vann or saving himself with the truth intact; he does both, splitting the ledger — half to prosecutors, half into the wind — and walks away owning nothing but the one thing he refused to sell.
about_author: Hazel Kavanagh spent nine years auditing shipping manifests for a maritime insurance syndicate before trading spreadsheets for sentences. She writes thrillers about people who discover that the numbers were never the point.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Jude. In Lisbon, Jude closes another immaculate case for Meridian Compliance Group, celebrated for work he knows is theater. A colleague's quiet warning — 'you certify what we tell you' — lands as an insult he can't refute. The beat is suffocating respectability: Jude realizes his integrity has become a product he sells by the hour.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: POV Jude. A burner phone appears in his desk drawer, no sender, one contact saved as E.V. When it rings, Elias Vann's voice — three years dead — says only 'Tangier, before the tide turns.' Jude verifies the voice against old interview tapes and finds it matches. The beat is vertigo: grief reopening as suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Suicide Note Didn't Say
chapters.summary: POV Jude, with a flashback interleave of Vann's final week. Jude reopens the closed file on Vann's death and finds the forensic report was signed off by his own current boss, Dana Okonkwo. The emotional beat is betrayal compounding betrayal — the past wasn't tragedy, it was housekeeping.

chapters.title: Tangier, Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Off-book, Jude flies to Tangier and finds Vann in a medina safehouse, thinner, paranoid, alive. Vann shows him fragments of the Halcyon Ledger — ten years of sanctions-busting routed through firms like Meridian. The beat is wary reunion: love for a mentor tangled with the question of why Vann waited three years to call.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jude/Vann. Vann wants extraction at dawn via a chartered flight out of Ibn Battuta; Jude notices the route is too clean, the contacts too cooperative. He tests a courier and watches the message get read in real time by someone else. The beat is dread crystallizing: the trap isn't around them, it's the plan itself.

chapters.title: Found Family, For Sale
chapters.summary: POV Vann. Vann's chapter reveals his motive isn't redemption but protection of the young analysts who inherited his network — including Jude. Meanwhile Dana calls Jude, offering promotion and silence, making clear she knows where he is. The beat is tenderness weaponized: everyone Jude loves is leverage.

chapters.title: Split the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Jude proposes the heresy: don't run with the whole ledger — copy it, scatter it, make it worthless as bait and unstoppable as truth. Vann resists; the full ledger is his life's proof. Their argument becomes the book's thematic core: loyalty to a man versus loyalty to what's true. The beat is rupture before resolve.

chapters.title: Dana's Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Dana Okonkwo. Her chapter humanizes the antagonist: she certified Vann's death under orders that came from above her, and she's been waiting three years for someone to give her a reason to defect too. She feeds Jude the real extraction window — which is not dawn. The beat is uneasy alliance across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Tarmac
chapters.summary: POV Jude. The false dawn flight is stormed; Jude and Vann take the real window Dana bought them, pursued through cargo corridors. On the runway, Vann is hit shielding Jude. Jude makes the choice: he uploads half the ledger mid-sprint to prosecutors worldwide and lets the physical drive burn with the plane. The beat is sacrifice as clarity.

chapters.title: Loose Debt
chapters.summary: POV Jude, weeks later. Vann survives, broken and free; the scattered ledger detonates investigations across four jurisdictions, and Meridian dissolves into subpoenas. Dana testifies; Jude refuses to return to compliance work of any kind. Closing image: Jude teaching financial literacy to kids in a Lisbon community center, finally handling money that means nothing and everything. The beat is earned lightness — debt paid forward, not collected.
